problem.text: Triangle $ABC$ has side-lengths $AB = 12$, $BC = 24$, and $AC = 18$. The line through the incenter of $\triangle ABC$ parallel to $\overline{BC}$ intersects $\overline{AB}$ at $M$ and $\overline{AC}$ at $N$. What is the perimeter of $\triangle AMN$?

steps.title: Where to start: draw the angle bisectors to the incenter
steps.body: The incenter $I$ is where the angle bisectors meet, and the line $MN$ is parallel to $BC$. Bisectors and parallel lines together make equal angles, so draw $BI$ and $CI$. Call $\angle ABC = 2b$ and $\angle ACB = 2c$; then $\angle MBI = b$ and $\angle NCI = c$. Since $MN \parallel BC$, corresponding angles give $\angle AMN = 2b$, so $\angle BMI = 180^\circ - 2b$.

your_turn.prompt: In triangle $BIM$, $\angle MBI = b$ and $\angle BMI = 180^\circ - 2b$. Find $\angle BIM$.

steps.title: Two isosceles triangles appear
steps.body: Triangle $BIM$ has two angles equal to $b$ (at $B$ and at $I$), so it is isosceles and $MI = MB$. The same argument at $C$ gives $\angle CIN = c = \angle NCI$.

your_turn.answer: $NC$, because the angles at $C$ and $I$ are both $c$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Let $MI = MB = x$ and $NI = NC = y$. Then $AM = 12 - x$, $AN = 18 - y$ and $MN = MI + IN = x + y$. The perimeter is $$(12 - x) + (18 - y) + (x + y) = 30,$$ which is just $AB + AC$; the side $BC = 24$ is never needed. The answer is **(B)**.

wrong_choices.A: This is half the perimeter of $\triangle ABC$ ($54 \div 2$), which you get by assuming $MN$ is the midsegment. But the incenter is not halfway up, so $M$ and $N$ are not midpoints.
